This page is generated from `schema/llmproxy-v0.schema.json`, the normative
schema for the file passed with `--config`. It lists every field, its type,
its default and whether it is required. For explanations and examples, see
[Configuration file](../configuration-file/).

Parsing is strict: an unknown field is a load error that names its full path.
Every string field accepts `${VAR_NAME}` environment-variable interpolation,
applied before parsing.

## Top level

The configuration format for llm-proxy. This file is the single source of truth for the v0 schema: user-facing documentation, editor autocomplete (yaml-language-server), and the config validator are all generated from it. Strings support environment-variable interpolation with `${VAR_NAME}`, applied before parsing. Parsing is strict: unknown fields are errors, never ignored. The top-level keys `envoy`, `tracing`, and `clusters` are RESERVED for future versions and rejected in v0.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | constant `0` | yes | none | Schema version. Must be 0. Future schema revisions bump this; llm-proxy refuses configs whose version it does not understand. |
| `listen` | [HostPort](#hostport) or [Listener](#listener) | no | `0.0.0.0:8080` | Where the proxy accepts client traffic. Shorthand string `host:port`, or an object to enable TLS. Default: `0.0.0.0:8080` (plaintext). Examples: `0.0.0.0:8080`, `{"address": "0.0.0.0:8443", "tls": {"cert_file": "/etc/llmproxy/tls.crt", "key_file": "/etc/llmproxy/tls.key"}}`. |
| `admin` | [HostPort](#hostport) | no | none | Admin/observability endpoint (`/ready`, `/config_dump`, `/clusters`, `/server_info`, `/stats`). `/stats` renders a flat text format, one `name: value` line per counter or histogram. Disabled when omitted. Bind to loopback unless you know why not. Examples: `127.0.0.1:9901`. |
| `auth` | [Auth](#auth) | no | none | Downstream authentication: verifies inbound requests carry a known virtual key or a valid JWT (`auth.jwt`) before any provider is reached. Fails CLOSED -- with this block present, a request with no recognized credential is refused (401), never admitted anonymously. Authorization is a separate axis: an authenticated tenant with no stored model policy is refused (403) unless `enforce.tenants_without_policy` is `allow`. Omit `auth` entirely to keep today's behavior (no application-level authentication). |
| `providers` | map of [Provider](#provider), keys match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; minimum entries 1 | yes | none | Named upstream LLM API providers. The key is the provider name referenced by `routes` (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Names `openai`, `anthropic`, and `openrouter` infer their `type` and `base_url` automatically — a working OpenAI provider is just `openai: { api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} }`. |
| `models` | map of [ModelDef](#modeldef), keys match `^([^*]+\*?\|\*)$` | no | `{}` | Logical model catalogue: a client-facing model name mapped to an ordered list of providers able to serve it -- e.g. Claude served by Anthropic directly or by Vertex, or Kimi-K2 served by Nebius. Each entry gets an implicit route matching its name, evaluated after `routes` and before the 404 backstop; `routes` still work unchanged. A key may be an exact model name, a single TRAILING wildcard (`gpt-4*`), or the bare catch-all `*` -- a `*` anywhere else (leading, mid-string, or more than one) is a load error, which is a narrower grammar than `routes[].model`'s (that one falls back to a general regex). Precedence when more than one key matches a request is total and exact match always wins, then the LONGEST matching prefix, then the bare `*` catch-all; two keys that could ever tie (a literal duplicate, since two distinct prefixes of equal length can never both match the same name) is a load error naming the duplicate. The providers are tried in order: `providers[0]` serves the request, and each later entry is a fallback with the same retry rules as `routes[].fallbacks`. With `weight` set on every entry, the first provider is picked in proportion to weight instead, and the other entries stay the fallback chain. Weighting spreads load across providers that serve the same model; it never changes the model. Cost-aware selection is not supported. Examples: `{"claude-sonnet-4-5": {"providers": ["anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929", {"provider": "vertex-us", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929", "dialect": "anthropic"}]}, "claude-*": {"providers": ["anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-latest"]}, "*": {"providers": ["openai/gpt-4o-mini"]}}`. |
| `routes` | array of [Route](#route); minimum items 0 | yes | none | Ordered routing rules, evaluated top to bottom — the FIRST rule whose `model` pattern matches the request wins (there is no specificity reordering; put specific patterns above broad ones). Requests matching no rule and no `models` entry get a 404 with a JSON error body listing known models. |
| `limits` | array of [Limit](#limit) | no | none | Rate limits and quotas. Every field is enforced as written. Each entry becomes one rule; a request must pass every rule that applies to it, and the first rule it exceeds rejects it with a 429 carrying `x-ratelimit-*` headers before the request is forwarded. Rule buckets are independent of the route. Token and request windows are one minute and epoch-aligned (they reset on the wall-clock minute, not a minute after first use). Token counts are extracted from provider responses, streaming included, and an admitted request already in flight is never truncated. Token and request counts reconcile with the store `auth.store` selects about once a second: with `auth.store: shared` replicas share them (and the fleet can admit a little over a limit between reconciles); with `in_memory` or `persistent`, or with no `auth:` block, each replica counts alone. Concurrent sessions follow the same rule: with `auth.store: shared` replicas share them through lease rows, and a replica that stops holds its slots for at most 5 seconds. |
| `observability` | [Observability](#observability) | no | none | Access logging, OTLP metric export, and OTLP trace export. Access log lines include token counts and TTFT/TPOT. Metrics are always served on the admin endpoint at `/stats` and `/stats/prometheus`, with no configuration here; `metrics` adds OTLP export of the same instruments. |
| `pricing` | [Pricing](#pricing) | no | none | Versioned LLM model rate card. Each completed request is priced in integer nanodollars using the meters of each entry's `basis`: all four text token buckets (plus optional image and audio token rates) for `tokens`, or a price per generated image for `images`. A `SIGHUP` reload installs a changed card, including one from a `price_list_file`, unless an `auth` section gives the chain a store: then the store holds the card and wins. The configured card seeds an empty store once, and neither a restart nor a reload replaces a stored card. `PUT /pricing` replaces the card at runtime. With `auth.store: shared` it reaches every replica within one policy poll; this is the only way replicas share a card. With `persistent` it survives a restart but stays on the replica that received it, because each replica owns its own file. With `in_memory`, or with no `auth` section, it is lost on restart. A card whose `effective_from` is in the future is refused. |
| `auto` | [AutoModel](#automodel) | no | none | Resolution of the reserved model name `auto`. A request whose `model` is `auto` is routed as the model this block selects: the tenant's entry in `tenants`, otherwise `default`. With no matching entry and no `default`, the request is refused with 400. Any other model name is routed unchanged. The provider's response is passed through unchanged, so its `model` field names the model the provider served, not `auto`. Access logs and usage records show both `auto` and the resolved model. While this block is set, `auto` is reserved: a `models` key or `routes[].model` of exactly `auto` is a load error. Absent means `auto` is an ordinary model name. Examples: `{"default": "gpt-4o-mini", "tenants": {"acme": "claude-sonnet"}}`. |
| `ledger` | [Ledger](#ledger) | no | none | The billing ledger: one durable, encrypted entry for every request dialled to a provider, including requests charged zero. An entry carries the request record, the amount charged to spend (or the list price on a route with no budget), the scopes charged, and an `instance_id`, a per-start `epoch` and a gapless `seq`. Each request reserves ledger capacity before it is dialled. When none is available (every slot held, the writer failed, or the spool at `max_disk_bytes`), `on_unavailable` decides what happens. Entries are committed in groups. A crash loses every entry not yet committed: normally the entries of about the last `group_commit_interval`, but while the spool is at `max_disk_bytes` the proxy holds entries in memory until an acknowledgement frees space, and a crash loses all of them. The bound in every case is `max_reservations` entries, since a slot is held until its entry commits. Committed entries are never evicted. The proxy needs a node id unique to this replica and stable across restarts (`--service-node`); it is the entries' `instance_id`. Absent means no ledger. Examples: `{"directory": "/var/lib/llm-proxy/ledger", "encryption_key_file": "/etc/llm-proxy/ledger.key", "encryption_key_id": "ledger-2026", "max_disk_bytes": 10737418240}`. |
| `guardrails` | [Guardrails](#guardrails) | no | none | Body-aware request checks. Each request with a body is sent to a check before any provider is dialled: its tenant's entry in `tenants`, otherwise `default`. The check receives the request body with the tenant and the requested and resolved model, and answers allow or deny. A denied request is refused with 403 and the check's reason; it is not dialled, not charged, not counted against a limit, and gets no ledger entry. The check only allows or denies; it never changes the request. Sending a request body to a check discloses every prompt to that service: point `url` only at a service trusted with them. Only a request that authentication and model authorization admit is sent. A request with an empty body is not checked. Each check adds one round trip to every checked request. Outcomes are counted in `llmproxy_guardrail_checks_total` and logged by `%LLM_GUARDRAIL%`. Absent means no request is checked. Examples: `{"default": {"http": {"url": "http://127.0.0.1:9000/check", "timeout": "500ms", "max_body_bytes": 1048576}, "failure_mode": "closed"}}`. |

Any other field is a load error.

Rules:

- At least one of these holds: `routes` has at least 1 item; or `models` is set and `models` has at least 1 entry.

## `Listener`

Used at: `listen`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | [HostPort](#hostport) | yes | none | A bind address in `host:port` form. IPv6 hosts use brackets: `[::1]:8080`. |
| `max_request_body_bytes` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 4294967295 | no | `1048576` | The largest request body the listener accepts, in bytes. A larger body gets `413`. Default: 1048576 (1 MiB). Raise it for long-context or image requests. The same value is the largest body that can be retried or fail over to another provider. Each in-flight request can hold up to this many bytes in memory. Lowers to the listener's `per_connection_buffer_limit_bytes`. Examples: `20971520`. |
| `max_connections` | integer; minimum 1 | no | `50000` | The most client connections the proxy holds open at once, across the whole process. Connections over the limit are closed on accept. Default: 50000 (Envoy's edge-proxy guidance). Must be greater than 0. Lowers to the bootstrap `overload_manager` monitor `envoy.resource_monitors.global_downstream_max_connections`. Examples: `10000`. |
| `request_headers_timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `10s` | Time allowed from the first byte of a request to its complete headers. Slow clients that exceed it are disconnected. Enforced for HTTP/1 only: on HTTP/2 the proxy logs one warning per process and does not enforce it. Default: 10s (Envoy's edge-proxy guidance). `0s` disables the timeout. Lowers to the HTTP connection manager's `request_headers_timeout`. |
| `request_timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `60s` | Time allowed to receive the whole request, headers and body. It does not bound the response, so long generations and streams are unaffected. Default: 60s (Envoy's edge-proxy guidance). `0s` disables the timeout. Raise it if clients upload very large bodies slowly. Lowers to the HTTP connection manager's `request_timeout`. |
| `stream_idle_timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `10m` | How long a request may go with no activity before it is cut. It bounds the wait for the provider's response headers (so a provider that accepts a request and never answers cannot hold the client and a concurrency permit forever). It does not bound the gap between response chunks: every rule carries its own `idle_timeout` (default 90s), which governs that gap once headers arrive. Default: 10m, long enough for a non-streaming generation that sends nothing until it finishes. `0s` disables the timeout. Lowers to the HTTP connection manager's `stream_idle_timeout`. |
| `max_stream_duration` | [Duration](#duration) | no | none | The longest a request may live, from receipt to the last response byte, however active the stream is. A cut stream that has already started answering ends without a clean finish. Default: no limit. `0s` also means no limit. Lowers to the HTTP connection manager's `common_http_protocol_options.max_stream_duration`. |
| `max_request_headers_kb` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 8192 | no | `60` | The largest request head accepted, in KiB. On HTTP/1.1 the head is the request line, every header line and the blank line that ends them; a larger head gets `431` and the connection is closed. On HTTP/2 the size is the name and value of every header, pseudo-headers included; a larger request has its stream reset. Default: 60 (Envoy's default). Raise it if clients send very large cookies or tokens. Lowers to the HTTP connection manager's `max_request_headers_kb`. Examples: `96`. |
| `max_request_headers_count` | integer; minimum 1 | no | `100` | The most headers a request may carry. On HTTP/1.1 a request with more gets `431` and the connection is closed. On HTTP/2 the count includes the pseudo-headers and each `cookie` header, and a request with more has its stream reset. Default: 100 (Envoy's default). Lowers to the HTTP connection manager's `common_http_protocol_options.max_headers_count`. Examples: `200`. |
| `tls` | [object](#listentls) | no | none | Terminate TLS for client connections. Nothing watches the certificate files. After a `SIGHUP` reload, the next accepted connection reads `cert_file` and `key_file` again, so a renewed certificate is served to new connections; existing connections keep the old one. A reload does not check the files: if one cannot be read, the listener resets every new TLS connection until a later reload succeeds, so check the files before you send `SIGHUP`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `Auth`

Used at: `auth`.

Downstream authentication. Exactly one of `hmac_secret` / `hmac_secret_file` is required -- mirrors the `api_key`/`api_key_file` choice on a `Provider`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hmac_secret` | string | no | none | The operator secret that keys the HMAC over virtual-key digests. Use `${ENV_VAR}` interpolation rather than inlining it. Fixed when the proxy starts: a `SIGHUP` reload that changes it is refused and the proxy keeps the running secret. Rotate it with a restart. Examples: `${LLMPROXY_AUTH_SECRET}`. |
| `hmac_secret_file` | string | no | none | Read the HMAC secret from this file (trailing whitespace trimmed). The file is read again on each `SIGHUP` reload, but the secret is fixed when the proxy starts: a reload that changes it is refused and the proxy keeps the running secret. Rotate it with a restart. |
| `keys` | array of [AuthKey](#authkey) | no | `[]` | Configured virtual keys. May be empty -- an `auth:` block with no keys authenticates nothing and therefore refuses every request (the correct fail-closed reading of "authentication is enabled, and no credential is valid"), which is legal but almost certainly a mistake, so it produces a load-time warning. The list is fixed when the proxy starts: a `SIGHUP` reload that adds, removes, or revokes a configured key is refused whole, so a change takes effect only after a restart. To revoke without a restart, use the admin API (`DELETE /tenants/{id}` revokes every key of a tenant, configured keys included). |
| `store` | [AuthStore](#authstore) | no | none | Where minted keys, revocations, and tenant policy live. Absent means `in_memory`, which keeps them only for the life of the process. Exactly one of the three shapes below, the same three the Envoy-mode `llmproxy.auth` filter accepts. The store is fixed at startup: a `SIGHUP` reload that changes it is refused, so changing it takes a restart. |
| `tenant_credentials` | [AuthTenantCredentials](#authtenantcredentials) | no | none | The key ring that seals tenant provider credentials at rest. Required when any `providers` entry sets `tenant_credentials: true`. Absent means the proxy cannot seal or open tenant credentials. Requires a durable `store`, `persistent` or `shared`; with `store` absent or `in_memory` this block is a load error. Fixed at startup: a `SIGHUP` reload that changes it, including new key bytes in a file at the same path, is refused. |
| `enforce` | [AuthEnforce](#authenforce) | no | none | Which tenant controls the proxy enforces when `auth` is set. Each defaults to `true`. Setting one to `false` removes that filter from the chain and logs a load-time warning; the matching admin writes (`PUT /tenants/{id}/policy`, `PUT /tenants/{id}/budget`, `PUT /tenants/{id}/limits`, `PUT /tenants/{id}/objects/{object_id}`) are then refused with 409. |
| `max_policy_staleness` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `4m` | How old this replica's copy of keys, revocations, and tenant policies may get while the store cannot be read. Before this age the last copy keeps serving; past it every virtual-key request is refused with 503 (`auth_policy_stale`) until the store answers again, because the copy may still hold a key revoked elsewhere. Whole seconds, at least `96s` (2 x the 48-second policy poll). The age is exported as `envoy_llmproxy_policy_snapshot_age_seconds`. |
| `stored_output_owner_ttl` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `720h` | How long the proxy keeps the owner of a stored response (`/v1/responses`) or a stored chat completion (`/v1/chat/completions` with `store: true`). These are created by inference requests, so their owners expire rather than accumulate. After the TTL the object is refused to every tenant, its creator included, until `PUT /tenants/{id}/objects/{object_id}` assigns it again; set it to at least the provider's retention. Whole seconds, at least `1s`. A load error with `enforce.object_ownership: false`, which omits the filter that reads it. |
| `jwt` | array of [AuthJwtProvider](#authjwtprovider) | no | `[]` | JWT/OIDC providers (ADR-0014). A `Bearer` value that is not a virtual key (`llmp_...`) is verified against the first entry whose `issuer` equals the token's `iss`. Only RS256 tokens with a `kid` header are accepted, with 60 seconds of clock skew. A token that is expired, not yet valid, wrongly signed, for another audience, or carries an unmapped tenant claim value gets 401. A verified token is admitted as the tenant its `tenant.values` entry names, and the user `jwt:<issuer>:<tenant>:<user claim>`. That tenant's model policy, budget, limits and object ownership apply exactly as for a virtual key; a token carries no grants of its own, so a mapped tenant with no stored model policy is refused (403) under the default `enforce.tenants_without_policy: deny`. JWT callers always use the operator's provider keys, never a tenant's stored provider credentials, so lowering warns when `tenant_credentials` is also set. May be combined with `keys`; with `jwt` set, `keys` may be empty without a warning. |
| `chargeback_tags` | [ChargebackTags](#chargebacktags) | no | none | Which chargeback tags a request may carry into its usage record and billing-ledger entry (`tags`), to attribute spend to a project, team or cost centre. Tags come from key metadata (`keys[].tags`, or the admin API's `POST /keys` and `PUT /keys/{id}/tags`) and, with `from_header: true`, from the `x-cost-tags` request header. A tag key that key metadata sets is never taken from the header, so a client cannot override the admin. A JWT caller has no key metadata and gets header tags only. Absent means no tags are attributed and the header is never read. Tags are never a metric label; dropped tags are counted in `envoy_llmproxy_chargeback_tags_dropped_total{reason}`. There is no tag budget. |

Any other field is a load error.

Rules:

- Set exactly one of `hmac_secret`, `hmac_secret_file`.

## `Provider`

Used at: `providers.<name>`.

One upstream LLM API. Exactly one of `api_key` / `api_key_file` may be set (omit both for unauthenticated local backends). Azure OpenAI requires `deployment` and `api_version`; Vertex requires project, location, publisher, and one OAuth access-token source; Bedrock requires region and AWS access-key and secret-key sources.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | one of `openai`, `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`, `openrouter`, `azure-openai`, `vertex`, `bedrock` | no | none | Provider API shape. `openrouter` uses OpenAI-compatible requests with cluster-owned /v1 to /api/v1 path rewriting. `openai-compatible` covers vLLM, Ollama, TGI, Together, and most self-hosted servers. Inferred for providers named `openai`, `anthropic`, or `openrouter`; defaults to `openai-compatible` otherwise. `azure-openai` uses Azure's deployment URL and `api-version` query parameter. `vertex` uses Google Cloud project/location/publisher settings and an OAuth access token; the proxy rewrites the request path to `/v1/projects/<project>/locations/<location>/publishers/<publisher>/models/<model>:streamRawPredict`. `bedrock` uses an AWS region and SigV4 credential sources; the proxy rewrites the request path to `/model/<model>/invoke` and signs the request. |
| `base_url` | string (uri) | no | none | API base URL. Required unless the provider name/type implies one (`openai` -> https://api.openai.com, `anthropic` -> https://api.anthropic.com, `openrouter` -> https://openrouter.ai). Examples: `http://vllm.internal:8000`, `https://api.together.xyz`. |
| `deployment` | string; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$` | no | none | Azure OpenAI deployment name. Required for `azure-openai`; used as a path segment. |
| `api_version` | string; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$` | no | none | Azure OpenAI API version query value. Required for `azure-openai`; sent as `api-version`. |
| `api_key` | string | no | none | API key, sent using provider type's native auth header (`api-key` for Azure OpenAI, `Authorization: Bearer` for other OpenAI-shaped APIs, `x-api-key` for Anthropic). Use `${ENV_VAR}` interpolation rather than inlining secrets. Examples: `${OPENAI_API_KEY}`. |
| `api_key_file` | string | no | none | Read the API key from this file (trailing whitespace trimmed). Nothing watches the file; a `SIGHUP` reload reads it again, and requests that start after the reload use the new key. Preferred over `api_key` for secret managers that mount files. |
| `project` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | Google Cloud project ID for Vertex AI. Required for `vertex`; rejected for other provider types. |
| `location` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | Google Cloud location for Vertex AI. Required for `vertex`; rejected for other provider types. |
| `publisher` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | Vertex AI publisher, such as `google` or `anthropic`. Required for `vertex`; rejected for other provider types. |
| `access_token` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | OAuth access token for Vertex AI, applied as is and never refreshed. Exactly one of `access_token` / `access_token_file` / `oauth2_jwt_bearer` is required for `vertex`. |
| `access_token_file` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | Read the Vertex OAuth access token from this file. Exactly one of `access_token` / `access_token_file` / `oauth2_jwt_bearer` is required for `vertex`. |
| `oauth2_jwt_bearer` | [object](#providersnameoauth2_jwt_bearer) | no | none | Mint and refresh the access token with the OAuth2 JWT-bearer grant (RFC 7523). The proxy signs an RS256 assertion with the key, exchanges it at `token_url`, and mints the next token `refresh_before` its expiry. With no unexpired token, a request to this provider moves to the next provider in its fallback chain, and `llmproxy_provider_credential_requests_total` counts it with `outcome=unavailable_failover`. With no next provider, the request gets a local 503 with the body `provider token unavailable`, counted with `outcome=unavailable`. Valid only for `vertex`. |
| `region` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | AWS region for Amazon Bedrock. Required for `bedrock`; rejected for other provider types. |
| `access_key_id` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | AWS access key ID for Bedrock SigV4. Exactly one of `access_key_id` / `access_key_id_file` is required for `bedrock`. |
| `access_key_id_file` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | Read the AWS access key ID from this file. Exactly one of `access_key_id` / `access_key_id_file` is required for `bedrock`. |
| `secret_access_key` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | AWS secret access key for Bedrock SigV4. Exactly one of `secret_access_key` / `secret_access_key_file` is required for `bedrock`. |
| `secret_access_key_file` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | Read the AWS secret access key from this file. Exactly one of `secret_access_key` / `secret_access_key_file` is required for `bedrock`. |
| `session_token` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | Optional AWS session token for Bedrock SigV4. If set, do not set `session_token_file`. |
| `session_token_file` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | Read an optional AWS session token from this file. If set, do not set `session_token`. |
| `extra_headers` | map of string | no | none | Additional headers to send on every request to this provider (e.g. org/project headers). Anthropic providers are sent a default `anthropic-version` automatically; setting it here overrides that default (header names are matched case-insensitively). |
| `ca_file` | string | no | none | PEM CA bundle for verifying this provider's TLS certificate. Only needed for self-hosted backends with private CAs; system roots are used otherwise. |
| `connect_timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `5s` | TCP/TLS connection establishment timeout for this provider. |
| `protocol` | one of `http1`, `http2` | no | `http1` | Upstream HTTP protocol for this provider's cluster. `http2` enables upstream connection reuse: each worker keeps up to 4 multiplexed connections to each address of this provider, dialling another when every open one carries 100 streams, instead of connecting fresh on every request. Most hosted providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, and most OpenAI-compatible APIs) support it; many local/self-hosted plaintext servers do not. Defaults to `http1`. |
| `tenant_credentials` | boolean | no | `false` | Let tenants with their own key for this provider send it instead of the operator key. Requires `auth.tenant_credentials`. Only header API-key provider types qualify: `openai`, `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`, `openrouter`, and `azure-openai`. `vertex` and `bedrock` are rejected. |
| `tenant_credential_verify_path` | string; pattern `^/` | no | none | Upstream path of the zero-cost GET that checks a tenant key when it is saved, e.g. `/api/v1/key`. Requires `tenant_credentials: true`. Defaults when unset and `base_url` is unset: `/api/v1/key` for `openrouter`, `/v1/models` for `openai` and `anthropic`; no default for other types, and none when `base_url` is set. Sent as is, without the cluster path rewrite. |
| `request_fields` | [object](#providersnamerequest_fields) | no | none | Generic top-level request-body field policy for this provider, enforced per attempt against whichever provider is actually dialled (so it holds on failover). A name must not appear in both lists. |
| `outlier_detection` | [object](#providersnameoutlier_detection) | no | none | Passive health checking. After `consecutive_5xx` consecutive failed attempts, the provider is ejected: a `models` entry passes it over, as primary or fallback, while another of its providers is not ejected, and serves from it again when the ejection ends. With every provider of the entry ejected, requests go to them in list order as without ejection. Ejection is per proxy process; replicas do not share it. Absent means the provider is never ejected. |

Any other field is a load error.

Rules:

- `api_key` and `api_key_file` are not both set.
- When `type` is `azure-openai`: `base_url`, `deployment`, `api_version` must be set.
- When `type` is not `azure-openai`: None of `deployment`, `api_version` is set.
- When `type` is `vertex`: `base_url`, `project`, `location`, `publisher` must be set. Exactly one of these holds: `access_token` is set and none of `access_token_file`, `oauth2_jwt_bearer` is set; or `access_token_file` is set and none of `access_token`, `oauth2_jwt_bearer` is set; or `oauth2_jwt_bearer` is set and none of `access_token`, `access_token_file` is set. None of `region`, `access_key_id`, `access_key_id_file`, `secret_access_key`, `secret_access_key_file`, `session_token`, `session_token_file`, `api_key`, `api_key_file` is set.
- When `type` is not `vertex`: None of `project`, `location`, `publisher`, `access_token`, `access_token_file`, `oauth2_jwt_bearer` is set.
- When `type` is `bedrock`: `base_url`, `region` must be set. None of `project`, `location`, `publisher`, `access_token`, `access_token_file`, `session_token` with `session_token_file`, `api_key`, `api_key_file` is set. Set exactly one of `access_key_id`, `access_key_id_file`. Set exactly one of `secret_access_key`, `secret_access_key_file`.
- When `type` is not `bedrock`: None of `region`, `access_key_id`, `access_key_id_file`, `secret_access_key`, `secret_access_key_file`, `session_token`, `session_token_file` is set.

## `ModelDef`

Used at: `models.<name>`.

One logical model and the providers able to serve it.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `providers` | array of [ProviderModelRef](#providermodelref) or [ModelProvider](#modelprovider); minimum items 1 | yes | none | Providers tried for this model, in priority order. Each entry is either the shorthand string form (`provider` or `provider/model`, reusing the same `ProviderModelRef` shape `routes` uses) or the object form, needed whenever `dialect` must be set explicitly. `providers[0]` serves the request; each later entry is a fallback, tried in order on a connection failure or a 429, 500, 502 or 503 response, never after the first response byte of a stream. With `weight` on every entry, each request picks its first provider in proportion to weight, and the other entries are its fallbacks in list order. A provider ejected by its `outlier_detection` is passed over while another entry has a provider that is not ejected. Every entry must speak the same dialect as `providers[0]`; a mismatch is a load error. |
| `max_output_tokens` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 4294967295 | no | none | Upper bound on the output tokens a request for this model may ask for. A request whose limit is larger is refused with a 400 naming the field and the cap; it is never lowered or rewritten. A limit that is not a non-negative integer, or a limit key repeated in the body, is also refused with a 400. A request that names no limit is forwarded unchanged. Each refusal adds 1 to `llmproxy_router_max_output_tokens_rejected_total`. The field checked follows the request path: `/responses` uses `max_output_tokens`, `/messages` uses `max_tokens`, and any other path (chat completions, completions) checks both `max_completion_tokens` and `max_tokens`. A body that is not JSON is forwarded unchanged. The cap follows the model the request names, so it cannot be combined with the `auto` block (a load error). Absent means no cap. Examples: `4096`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `Route`

Used at: `routes[]`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | [ModelPattern](#modelpattern) | yes | none | A glob matched against the request's `model` field (the JSON body field for chat/completions APIs; the `model` query parameter for realtime WebSocket endpoints). `*` matches any run of characters; matching is case-sensitive. `*` alone matches every request. |
| `provider` | [ProviderModelRef](#providermodelref) | yes | none | Where matching requests go. The `provider/model` form does not rewrite the model yet; see `ProviderModelRef`. |
| `fallbacks` | array of [ProviderModelRef](#providermodelref) | no | none | Tried in order when the primary provider fails (connection failure, or a 429, 500, 502 or 503 response — and never after the first response byte of a stream has been sent to the client), or when the primary's credential cannot be applied (no unexpired minted token, a failed Bedrock signature). A credential failure moves to the next provider without using a retry. Each fallback gets a fresh attempt with the same request body. Every fallback must speak the same dialect as the primary; a mismatch is a load error. The `provider/model` form does not rewrite the model yet; see `ProviderModelRef`. |
| `retries` | [object](#routesretries) | no | none | Retry policy for this route. Defaults are LLM-safe: retry only what is certainly unserved (connection failures, 429s, and 5xx received before any response byte); a request is never replayed once streaming to the client has begun. NOT a separate budget from `fallbacks` -- both draw on one retry count, and each retry against a fallback chain moves to the NEXT member rather than repeating the primary. |
| `idle_timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `90s` | Maximum time with NO bytes flowing (between response chunks / SSE events / WebSocket frames). There is deliberately no total-duration timeout by default — LLM generations and realtime sessions are long-lived; idle-based timeouts are the correct guard. `0s` disables the idle timeout for this route. |
| `streaming` | one of `strict` | no | none | Assert that every configured HTTP filter for this route flushes response bytes through. Configuration loading fails if any installed filter can buffer a response; omit this field for the normal streaming-by-default behavior. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `Limit`

Used at: `limits[]`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string; pattern `^(global\|client-ip\|tenant\|header:[A-Za-z0-9-]+)$` | yes | none | What the limit is counted against: `global` (one bucket for all traffic), `client-ip` (one bucket per TCP peer address; behind a load balancer that is the balancer's address, because the dialect has no trusted-hops setting), `tenant` (one bucket per authenticated tenant -- requires an `auth:` block; configuring this without one is a load error, since nothing would authenticate a tenant), or `header:<name>` (one bucket per distinct value of the named request header, e.g. `header:x-api-key` for per-caller quotas). The header value is hashed, never stored or logged raw, and a request without that header is not counted against this limit. `header:authorization` buckets per credential: on the hashed `authorization` value, or, when `auth:` has verified and removed that header, on the authenticated virtual key (one bucket per key, so two keys of one tenant are counted apart); write `tenant` to bucket on the authenticated tenant. Examples: `header:authorization`, `tenant`, `global`, `client-ip`, `header:x-api-key`. |
| `tokens_per_minute` | [TokenAmount](#tokenamount) | no | none | Total (input + output) tokens allowed per one-minute epoch-aligned window per bucket. Usage is extracted from provider responses, including streamed ones; enforcement is at request admission (the request that would exceed the budget is rejected; in-flight streams are never truncated). Enforced for every key. |
| `requests_per_minute` | [TokenAmount](#tokenamount) | no | none | Requests allowed per one-minute epoch-aligned window per bucket. Counted at admission, for every key. |
| `concurrent_sessions` | integer; minimum 1 | no | none | Maximum streams in flight per bucket (an active request/response stream, including SSE; released when the stream ends). Enforced at admission, so the 429 happens before the stream starts, never mid-stream. Values above 4294967295 are a load error. Examples: `10`. |
| `models` | array of [ModelPattern](#modelpattern) | no | none | Restrict this limit to requests whose model matches one of these patterns (an exact name or a single trailing `*`). Omit to apply to all traffic. Requests for other models neither count against nor are rejected by this limit. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `Observability`

Used at: `observability`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `access_logs` | [object](#observabilityaccess_logs) | no | none | Where and how per-request/per-session access log entries are written. |
| `force_usage_reporting` | boolean | no | `true` | Forces `stream_options.include_usage` onto every streaming OpenAI-dialect request, including ones where the client asked for no usage, so token usage is always logged/accounted for streamed responses. This makes the provider emit one extra final SSE frame carrying usage; well-behaved SDKs handle it, but a hand-rolled client that iterates `choices[0]` without a guard can trip over that frame. Set to `false` for strict passthrough if that's a concern. Examples: `true`, `false`. |
| `metrics` | [object](#observabilitymetrics) | no | none | OTLP metric export. Independent of `tracing`: set this without `tracing` to export metrics with tracing fully off, and note that turning tracing off does not stop metrics. Omit entirely for no OTLP metric export -- which does not disable `/stats/prometheus`, which works with no OTLP configuration at all. `export_deadline` must be shorter than `export_interval`, or every export is abandoned as a timeout before the next one is due. |
| `traces` | [Traces](#traces) | no | none | Trace export: one record per request (request and response bodies, size-capped; no headers) for tenants that opt in through tenant policy, written to a local directory as compressed JSON-lines segments and optionally uploaded to S3-compatible storage. Requires the top-level `auth` block, since without tenants nothing can opt in. Boot-scoped: a reload that changes it is refused and the previous configuration keeps serving. Needs a node id unique to this replica (`--service-node`). Omit for no trace export. |
| `tracing` | [object](#observabilitytracing) | no | none | OTLP trace export. With this block set, the proxy exports spans to `otlp_endpoint`; omit it to keep tracing off. An inbound `traceparent`'s sampled bit is always honored regardless of `sample_ratio`; the ratio only applies when this proxy mints a new root span. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `Pricing`

Used at: `pricing`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `catalog` | object | no | none | Public source pricing metadata exposed by the admin pricing inventory; never used as token rates. |
| `price_list_file` | string | no | none | A file holding one price list, in YAML or JSON, with the same fields as `price_list`. Read at startup and on each reload; a file the proxy cannot read is a load error naming it. |
| `price_list` | [PriceList](#pricelist) | no | none | The price list, written inline. |

Any other field is a load error.

Rules:

- Set exactly one of `price_list_file`, `price_list`.

## `AutoModel`

Used at: `auto`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | The model for a tenant with no entry in `tenants`, and for a request with no authenticated tenant. Must be a concrete model name (no `*`, not `auto`) that a `routes` rule or `models` entry serves. Absent means such a request is refused with 400. Examples: `gpt-4o-mini`. |
| `tenants` | map of string | no | none | Tenant -> model. A tenant is the `tenant` an `auth.keys` entry (or a minted key) authenticates as. Requires an `auth` block. Each model must be a concrete model name that a `routes` rule or `models` entry serves. Examples: `{"acme": "claude-sonnet", "globex": "gpt-4o"}`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `Ledger`

Used at: `ledger`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `directory` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | Absolute path of the ledger spool directory. Created owner-only (0700) if absent; an existing directory must be owner-only. One proxy process writes it at a time. |
| `encryption_key_file` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | Absolute path of the key new entries are sealed under: a 0600 file holding exactly 32 raw bytes. Read at startup; a missing or unreadable key stops the proxy from starting. |
| `encryption_key_id` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | Names `encryption_key_file`'s key, at most 128 bytes. Stored beside each entry so the right key opens it. |
| `previous_keys` | array of [LedgerKey](#ledgerkey) | no | `[]` | Retired keys, at most 31, kept decrypt-only so entries sealed before a key rotation still open. Ids must be unique across this list and `encryption_key_id`. |
| `max_disk_bytes` | integer; minimum 2097152, maximum 1099511627776 | yes | none | Disk budget for the spool. At this cap new requests follow `on_unavailable`, and committed entries are never evicted to make room. Only an acknowledgement (`POST /ledger/ack`) frees space; once it does, the entries held at the cap are written and requests are admitted again without a restart. |
| `max_reservations` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 1048576 | no | `16384` | Ledger slots: requests in flight plus entries not yet committed. A request holds its slot from admission until its entry is committed. With every slot held, new requests follow `on_unavailable`. |
| `group_commit_max_entries` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 4096 | no | `512` | A group of entries is committed when it reaches this size or `group_commit_interval`, whichever comes first. |
| `group_commit_interval` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `50ms` | The longest an entry waits to be committed while the spool has space. It bounds what a crash loses only then: at `max_disk_bytes` entries are held in memory until an acknowledgement, and a crash loses all of them. Bounded to 1ms-1s. |
| `on_unavailable` | one of `reject`, `admit` | no | `reject` | What a request gets when no ledger capacity is available. `reject`: a local 503 naming the reason (`queue_full`, `writer_failed` or `disk_full`), counted in `llmproxy_ledger_rejected_total`; no request reaches a provider unledgered, so ledger health becomes availability. `admit`: the request is served without an entry, counted in `llmproxy_ledger_unledgered_total` and warned about at most once every 5 seconds. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `Guardrails`

Used at: `guardrails`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | [GuardrailCheck](#guardrailcheck) | yes | none | The check for a tenant with no entry in `tenants`, and for a request with no authenticated tenant. Required: there is no unchecked default. |
| `tenants` | map of [GuardrailCheck](#guardrailcheck) | no | none | Tenant -> check, replacing `default` for that tenant. A tenant is the `tenant` an `auth.keys` entry (or a minted key) authenticates as. Requires an `auth` block. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `listen.tls`

Terminate TLS for client connections. Nothing watches the certificate files. After a `SIGHUP` reload, the next accepted connection reads `cert_file` and `key_file` again, so a renewed certificate is served to new connections; existing connections keep the old one. A reload does not check the files: if one cannot be read, the listener resets every new TLS connection until a later reload succeeds, so check the files before you send `SIGHUP`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cert_file` | string | yes | none | Path to the PEM certificate chain. |
| `key_file` | string | yes | none | Path to the PEM private key. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `AuthKey`

Used at: `auth.keys[]`.

One virtual key. The plaintext key never appears in configuration -- only a keyed digest of it.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | Names this credential in audit logs and in the access log's response-code details. Must be unique within `auth.keys`. Examples: `alice-laptop`. |
| `tenant` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | The tenant (account/team) this key authenticates as. Several keys may share a tenant; that's the normal case -- revoking one leaked key must not revoke the whole account. Examples: `acme`. |
| `digest` | string; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` | yes | none | Lowercase hex of `HMAC-SHA256(hmac_secret, <plaintext key>)`, exactly 64 characters -- the plaintext is shown to the operator once, at creation, and is never recoverable from configuration. Generate both together with `llm-proxy --mode keygen --tenant <tenant> --key-id <id>` (reads the same secret via `--hmac-secret-file`/`$LLMPROXY_AUTH_SECRET`, and prints a ready-to-paste `id`/`tenant`/`digest` block). If you have no `llm-proxy` binary handy, `openssl` computes the same digest (note `printf %s`, not a here-string -- `<<<` appends a trailing newline that changes the digest): `printf %s "llmp_yourkey" \| openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$LLMPROXY_AUTH_SECRET" -hex` Examples: `3f2a1e9c7b4d5f6a8e0c2b1d4f6a8c0e2b4d6f8a0c2e4b6d8f0a2c4e6b8d0f2a`. |
| `revoked` | boolean | no | `false` | A revoked key is refused, distinguished from an unknown key in the access log's response-code details (`auth_revoked_key` vs `auth_unknown_key`) but NOT on the wire -- both produce an identical 401, so a caller can't learn from the response alone whether a key they guessed was ever valid. |
| `tags` | map of string | no | `{}` | Chargeback tags for requests this key authenticates (key metadata). At most 32. Keys follow `chargeback_tags.allowed[].key`; values are 1 to 256 bytes of ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `:`, `/`, `@`, `+` and `-`. `auth.chargeback_tags` decides which are attributed. A change applies on restart, like any change to `keys`. Examples: `{"team": "infra", "project": "search"}`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `AuthStore`

Used at: `auth.store`.

Exactly one of `in_memory`, `persistent`, or `shared`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `in_memory` | object | no | none | Keys and policy live only for the life of the process. Takes no fields. |
| `persistent` | [AuthStorePersistent](#authstorepersistent) | no | none | Keys, policy and the rate card survive a restart in an embedded `redb` file. The file is created if missing and takes a lock, so one process owns it at a time: replicas do not share it. |
| `shared` | [AuthStoreShared](#authstoreshared) | no | none | Keys, policy and the rate card are shared by every replica through Redis. Exactly one of `url` / `url_file` is required -- a Redis URL may embed a password, so it belongs in the environment or a mounted file, same as `hmac_secret`. Requires `--service-node`: each replica needs a node id that is unique and stable across restarts, and the dialect has no field for it, so without the flag this block is a load error at `auth.store.shared`. |

Any other field is a load error.

Rules:

- Set exactly one of `in_memory`, `persistent`, `shared`.

## `AuthTenantCredentials`

Used at: `auth.tenant_credentials`.

Key-encryption keys that seal tenant provider credentials at rest. Each key is a 0600 file holding exactly 32 raw bytes. Required when any provider sets `tenant_credentials: true`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `encryption_key_file` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | Path to the key that new tenant credentials are sealed under. Read by the proxy at startup; the key bytes never appear in configuration. |
| `encryption_key_id` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | Names `encryption_key_file`'s key. It is stored in plaintext beside each sealed credential so the proxy can pick the right key to open it. |
| `previous_keys` | array of [AuthTenantCredentialKey](#authtenantcredentialkey) | no | `[]` | Retired keys, kept decrypt-only so credentials sealed before a key rotation still open. Ids must be unique across this list and `encryption_key_id`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `AuthEnforce`

Used at: `auth.enforce`.

Which tenant controls the proxy enforces when `auth` is set. Each defaults to `true`. Setting one to `false` removes that filter from the chain and logs a load-time warning; the matching admin writes (`PUT /tenants/{id}/policy`, `PUT /tenants/{id}/budget`, `PUT /tenants/{id}/limits`, `PUT /tenants/{id}/objects/{object_id}`) are then refused with 409.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model_policy` | boolean | no | `true` | Enforce per-tenant model allow-lists set through the admin API (`llmproxy.model_authz`). What a tenant with no stored policy may use is `tenants_without_policy`. |
| `spend` | boolean | no | `true` | Enforce per-tenant and per-key spend budgets (`llmproxy.spend_limit`). Cost comes from the `pricing` rate card. |
| `limits` | boolean | no | `true` | Enforce tenant and key rate limits set through the admin API (`PUT /tenants/{id}/limits`, `PUT /keys/{id}/limits`): tokens per minute, requests per minute and concurrent streams. A key only narrows its tenant: a request must pass both. With `auth.store: shared` the counters and concurrent streams are shared by every replica; with another store each replica counts alone, so N replicas admit up to N times a limit. With `false` and no `limits` entry, `llmproxy.token_limit` is omitted; a `limits` entry still adds it, and it then enforces these limits too. |
| `object_ownership` | boolean | no | `true` | Keep provider objects to the tenant that created them (`llmproxy.object_ownership`): files, batches (`/v1/files`, `/v1/batches`, `/v1/messages/batches`), responses, stored chat completions, uploads, vector stores, fine-tuning jobs, assistants, threads, containers and conversations. Every tenant reaches a provider through one provider account, so the proxy records which tenant created each object and answers 404, without dialling the provider, to a request that names an object the caller's tenant does not own, or that no tenant owns. Listing a collection is refused with 404. An object named in a JSON request body (`file_id` and other `*_file_id` or `*_file_ids` members, `training_file`, `validation_file`, `previous_response_id`, `vector_store_ids`, `assistant_id`, `thread_id`, `container`, `conversation`; not inside `metadata`) must be the caller's too. A body that could spell one but is not valid JSON gets 400. A chat completion is recorded only with `store: true`, and a response unless `store: false`; their owners expire after `auth.stored_output_owner_ttl`. Owners are stored in `auth.store`: with `persistent` they survive a restart, and with `shared` every replica sees them. With `in_memory` they are lost on restart, and the proxy then refuses those objects as unknown. If the store cannot answer, the request gets 503. Fine-tuned models are not objects: grant them per tenant in model policy, since `access: all` reaches every tenant's fine-tuned models. `false` omits the filter and logs a load-time warning; any tenant can then reach the objects of any other tenant. |
| `tenants_without_policy` | one of `deny`, `allow` | no | `deny` | What an authenticated tenant with no stored model policy may use. `deny` (the default) refuses every model with 403 until `PUT /tenants/{id}/policy` grants some; the first refusal per tenant is logged. `allow` grants every model and logs a load-time warning. A load error with `model_policy: false`, which omits the filter that reads it. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `AuthJwtProvider`

Used at: `auth.jwt[]`.

One JWT issuer. Every field is required.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | The token's `iss` must equal this exactly. Unique within `auth.jwt`. Examples: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/9f1c0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/v2.0`. |
| `audience` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | The token's `aud` must contain this value. A token without `aud` is refused. Examples: `api://llm-proxy`. |
| `jwks` | [AuthJwtJwks](#authjwtjwks) | yes | none | Where the issuer's signing keys come from: exactly one of `discovery_url` or `keys`. |
| `tenant` | [AuthJwtTenant](#authjwttenant) | yes | none | Which claim names the tenant, and which claim values are admitted as which tenant. |
| `user` | [AuthJwtUser](#authjwtuser) | yes | none | Which claim names the user. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `ChargebackTags`

Used at: `auth.chargeback_tags`.

The operator's chargeback-tag allow-list and caps. Tags that fail it are dropped and counted by reason: `not_allowed` (key not listed, or value not one of its `values`), `too_long` (over `max_value_bytes`), `over_count` (over `max_tags`; key-metadata tags fill the cap first), `malformed` (the header did not parse; all its tags are dropped and the request is still served) and `overridden` (the header set a key that key metadata sets).

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allowed` | array of [ChargebackAllowedTag](#chargebackallowedtag); minimum items 1 | yes | none | The tag keys that may be attributed. |
| `from_header` | boolean | no | `false` | Read tags from the `x-cost-tags` request header, written as comma-separated `key=value` pairs (`project=search,team=infra`). The header is removed before the request goes upstream. False means the header is never read and is forwarded unchanged. |
| `max_tags` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 32 | no | `8` | Most tags on one request. |
| `max_value_bytes` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 256 | no | `64` | Longest tag value, in bytes. A longer value is dropped as `too_long`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `providers.<name>.oauth2_jwt_bearer`

Mint and refresh the access token with the OAuth2 JWT-bearer grant (RFC 7523). The proxy signs an RS256 assertion with the key, exchanges it at `token_url`, and mints the next token `refresh_before` its expiry. With no unexpired token, a request to this provider moves to the next provider in its fallback chain, and `llmproxy_provider_credential_requests_total` counts it with `outcome=unavailable_failover`. With no next provider, the request gets a local 503 with the body `provider token unavailable`, counted with `outcome=unavailable`. Valid only for `vertex`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `token_url` | string; pattern `^https?://[^/?#@]+` | yes | none | Token endpoint. Must be `https`; plain `http` is accepted only to a loopback host. |
| `issuer` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | JWT `iss`, for example a service account's email address. |
| `subject` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | JWT `sub`, when the grant impersonates another principal. |
| `key_id` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | JWT header `kid`. |
| `private_key_file` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | RSA private key, PKCS#8 PEM (`BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`). Read and checked at every load; a bad key is a load error. |
| `scopes` | array of string; minimum items 1 | yes | none | Scopes, joined with spaces into the JWT `scope` claim. |
| `audience` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | JWT `aud`. Defaults to `token_url`. |
| `assertion_lifetime` | [Duration](#duration) | no | none | `exp - iat` of each assertion, whole seconds from 1s to 24h. Default `1h`. |
| `refresh_before` | [Duration](#duration) | no | none | Mint the next token this long before the current one expires, whole seconds from 1s to 24h. Default `5m`. |
| `timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | no | none | Bounds one token request, connect included, whole seconds from 1s to 24h. Default `10s`. |
| `ca_file` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | PEM bundle that verifies an `https` token endpoint instead of the platform roots. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `providers.<name>.request_fields`

Generic top-level request-body field policy for this provider, enforced per attempt against whichever provider is actually dialled (so it holds on failover). A name must not appear in both lists.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deny` | array of string; items unique | no | none | Top-level body keys that make the request fail with 400 `request_field_not_permitted`. |
| `strip` | array of string; items unique | no | none | Top-level body keys removed before the request is sent to this provider. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `providers.<name>.outlier_detection`

Passive health checking. After `consecutive_5xx` consecutive failed attempts, the provider is ejected: a `models` entry passes it over, as primary or fallback, while another of its providers is not ejected, and serves from it again when the ejection ends. With every provider of the entry ejected, requests go to them in list order as without ejection. Ejection is per proxy process; replicas do not share it. Absent means the provider is never ejected.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `consecutive_5xx` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 4294967295 | no | `5` | Consecutive failed attempts that eject the provider. A failure is a 5xx response or a local failure (connection refused, reset, or timeout). A 429 or any other response ends the run. |
| `base_ejection_time` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `30s` | Length of the first ejection. Each later ejection of the provider lasts this value times the number of ejections so far, up to `max_ejection_time`. Must be greater than 0. |
| `max_ejection_time` | [Duration](#duration) | no | none | Upper bound on one ejection. Default: the larger of `300s` and `base_ejection_time`. Must not be less than `base_ejection_time`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `ModelProvider`

Used at: `models.<name>.providers[]`.

The object form of a `models.<name>.providers` entry, needed whenever `dialect` must be explicit -- the shorthand string form (`provider` or `provider/model`) cannot carry it.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | string; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` | yes | none | Key into `providers`. Examples: `anthropic`, `vertex-us`, `nebius`. |
| `model` | string | no | none | Upstream model ID at this provider, if different from the model's own catalogue name (e.g. Anthropic's dated model IDs, or a Vertex publisher-model path). The proxy writes it into the request body's `model` field for the provider that serves the attempt (and into the path for `vertex` and `bedrock`); after a fallback, the next provider gets its own value. Examples: `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct`. |
| `dialect` | one of `openai`, `anthropic` | no | none | Wire format this provider entry speaks. Optional (and derived from the provider's `type`) for `openai`/`anthropic`/`openai-compatible`/`azure-openai`, whose wire format the type alone determines. REQUIRED for `vertex`/`bedrock`, which serve more than one wire format under a single provider type -- e.g. Vertex hosts Anthropic-shaped Claude, Google-shaped Gemini, and OpenAI-shaped Kimi. Omitting it there is a load error naming the field, never a guess: the wrong parser can partially match the wrong body shape and bill usage against a number nobody computed. The shorthand string form cannot express this field at all, so an ambiguous-type provider used here must use this object form. Examples: `anthropic`. |
| `weight` | integer; minimum 0, maximum 1000000 | no | none | Share of this model's requests that start at this provider. Set it on every entry of `providers` or on none; a mix is a load error, and the shorthand string form cannot carry it. The first provider of each request is picked once, in proportion to weight, from the entries whose weight is above 0. The remaining entries are that request's fallbacks, in list order, with the same retry rules as without weights. `0` makes an entry a fallback only. The weights must not all be 0, and a provider must not appear twice in a weighted list. A provider ejected by its `outlier_detection` gets no first picks until the ejection ends: its share goes to the next entry in list order that is not ejected. The pick is random per request, so the split matches the weights over many requests, not over a few. It is the same on every worker and is not coordinated across replicas. Absent on every entry means `providers[0]` serves and the rest are fallbacks. Examples: `3`, `1`, `0`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `routes[].retries`

Retry policy for this route. Defaults are LLM-safe: retry only what is certainly unserved (connection failures, 429s, and 5xx received before any response byte); a request is never replayed once streaming to the client has begun. NOT a separate budget from `fallbacks` -- both draw on one retry count, and each retry against a fallback chain moves to the NEXT member rather than repeating the primary.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attempts` | integer; minimum 0, maximum 5 | no | `1` | Extra attempts (0 disables retries). On a route with `fallbacks`, retries walk the chain instead of repeating the primary, and the emitted retry count is raised to whichever is larger -- this value, or the number needed to reach the last fallback -- so 0 does NOT disable failover there. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `observability.access_logs`

Where and how per-request/per-session access log entries are written.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `output` | string | no | `stdout` | `stdout`, `stderr`, or a file path. Streamed responses and realtime sessions are logged once at stream end with usage totals. Examples: `stdout`, `/var/log/llmproxy/access.log`. |
| `format` | one of `text`, `json` | no | `text` | `json` emits one structured object per line (recommended for log pipelines). |

Any other field is a load error.

## `observability.metrics`

OTLP metric export. Independent of `tracing`: set this without `tracing` to export metrics with tracing fully off, and note that turning tracing off does not stop metrics. Omit entirely for no OTLP metric export -- which does not disable `/stats/prometheus`, which works with no OTLP configuration at all. `export_deadline` must be shorter than `export_interval`, or every export is abandoned as a timeout before the next one is due.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `otlp_endpoint` | string | yes | none | The OTLP/gRPC collector endpoint for metrics. May differ from the tracing one. Examples: `http://localhost:4317`. |
| `service_name` | string | no | `llm-proxy` | OTLP resource attribute `service.name`. |
| `export_interval` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `15s` | How often to snapshot and export the registry. Each export is a full cumulative snapshot, so this trades collector bandwidth against freshness. Bounded to 1s-1h. |
| `export_deadline` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `10s` | Per-export deadline. This is what bounds a collector that accepts a connection and then stops responding, rather than merely retrying it. Must be less than `export_interval`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `Traces`

Used at: `observability.traces`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `directory` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | Absolute path of the segment directory. Created owner-only (0700). One proxy process uses it at a time; a second is refused at startup. |
| `max_disk_bytes` | integer; minimum 1048576, maximum 1125899906842624 | yes | none | Budget for every segment on disk, open or sealed, uploaded or not. Must be at least 2 x max_open_segments x segment_max_bytes. At the cap the oldest unsent segment is dropped and counted. |
| `max_age` | [Duration](#duration) | no | none | Directory destination only (rejected with `s3`, whose objects expire by the bucket's lifecycle rules): sealed segments older than this are deleted. Bounded to 10 years. |
| `codec` | one of `gzip`, `zstd` | no | `gzip` | Segment compression. `gzip` is read by every warehouse loader; `zstd` needs a consumer that reads long-window zstd. |
| `zstd_window_log` | integer; minimum 20, maximum 27 | no | `24` | log2 of the zstd window. Only with `codec: zstd`. max_open_segments x 2^zstd_window_log must not exceed 2 GiB. |
| `max_request_body_bytes` | integer; minimum 1024, maximum 67108864 | no | `1048576` | Per-request cap on the captured request body. |
| `max_response_body_bytes` | integer; minimum 1024, maximum 67108864 | no | `4194304` | Per-request cap on the captured response body. |
| `max_memory_bytes` | integer; minimum 1048576, maximum 1099511627776 | no | `268435456` | Global cap on every retained body byte, in flight and queued. Must be at least max_request_body_bytes + max_response_body_bytes. |
| `max_queued_traces` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 1048576 | no | `4096` | Global cap on captures in flight plus queued. |
| `segment_max_bytes` | integer; minimum 1048576, maximum 1073741824 | no | `67108864` | A segment is sealed when its compressed size reaches this. Must be at least the largest line: both body caps base64-expanded, plus 1 MiB. |
| `segment_max_age` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `5m` | A segment is sealed when it is this old. Bounded to 10s-1h. |
| `max_open_segments` | integer; minimum 1, maximum 4096 | no | `64` | Open (tenant, date) segments; the least recently used is sealed beyond this. |
| `s3` | [TracesS3](#tracess3) | no | none | An S3-compatible upload destination. Sealed segments are uploaded, then deleted locally. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `observability.tracing`

OTLP trace export. With this block set, the proxy exports spans to `otlp_endpoint`; omit it to keep tracing off. An inbound `traceparent`'s sampled bit is always honored regardless of `sample_ratio`; the ratio only applies when this proxy mints a new root span.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `otlp_endpoint` | string | yes | none | The OTLP/gRPC collector endpoint. Examples: `http://localhost:4317`. |
| `service_name` | string | no | `llm-proxy` | OTLP resource attribute `service.name`. |
| `export_deadline` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `5s` | Per-export deadline for trace-batch RPCs. Bounds a collector that accepts the connection and then stops responding: each hung attempt costs one timeout, never an indefinite stall. Bounded to 100ms-60s. |
| `sample_ratio` | number; minimum 0.0, maximum 1.0 | no | `1.0` | Head-sampling ratio for a newly minted root span (no inbound `traceparent`, or one that arrives unsampled). |

Any other field is a load error.

The proxy sends `POST <url>` with a JSON object: `tenant`, `requested_model` and `resolved_model` (each a string or null) and `body`, the request body as text, or `body_base64` instead when the body is not UTF-8. Required: there is no default. |

## `AuthJwtJwks`

Used at: `auth.jwt[].jwks`.

Where the issuer's signing keys come from: exactly one of `discovery_url` or `keys`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `discovery_url` | string; pattern `^https://[^/]` | no | none | OIDC discovery document URL (`.../.well-known/openid-configuration`). A background thread fetches it, follows its `jwks_uri`, and refreshes the key set every `refresh_interval`; requests never wait on it. Until the first fetch succeeds every token from this issuer is refused. A failed refresh logs a warning and keeps the last key set; after 6 missed refreshes (`6 x refresh_interval`) the set is stale and every token from this issuer is refused (401) until a refresh succeeds. |
| `refresh_interval` | [Duration](#duration) | no | `10m` | How often the key set is refreshed. Whole seconds, at least `1s`. Only with `discovery_url`. |
| `trusted_ca_file` | string; minimum length 1 | no | none | PEM bundle of CA certificates trusted for the discovery and JWKS fetches instead of the system roots. Only with `discovery_url`. |
| `keys` | array of [AuthJwtKey](#authjwtkey); minimum items 1 | no | none | A static key set, copied from the issuer's JWKS document. Never refreshed. |

Any other field is a load error.

Rules:

- Exactly one of these holds: `discovery_url` is set and `keys` is not set; or `keys` is set and none of `discovery_url`, `refresh_interval`, `trusted_ca_file` is set.

## `AuthJwtTenant`

Used at: `auth.jwt[].tenant`.

Which claim names the tenant, and which claim values are admitted as which tenant.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |

| `claim` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | The claim whose string value selects the tenant, for example Entra's `tid`. A token without it is refused. Examples: `tid`. |
| `values` | map of string; minimum entries 1 | yes | none | Claim value -> llm-proxy tenant. A token whose claim value is not listed is refused (401); a claim value is never used as a tenant name directly. A tenant must not be `default`, must not contain `:`, and must be short enough that `jwt:<issuer>:<tenant>:` leaves 36 bytes of the 128-byte user id for the user claim. A longer user id makes the proxy drop that request's usage record, so keep user claims to 36 bytes or fewer (Entra's `oid` is 36). Examples: `{"9f1c0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000": "acme"}`. |

Any other field is a load error.

## `PriceEntry`

Used at: `pricing.price_list.entries[]`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `basis` | one of `tokens`, `images`, `characters`, `audio_seconds` | no | `tokens` | What the entry prices. `tokens`: text, and optionally image and audio, tokens, priced by `tier_mode` and `tiers`. `images`: each image a generation or edit returned, priced by `image_prices`. `characters`: each character of a speech request's `input`, priced by `nanodollars_per_character`; it is charged only when the response status is 2xx. `audio_seconds`: the audio duration a transcription or translation response reports, priced by `nanodollars_per_second`. An entry that is not `tokens` sets neither `tier_mode` nor `tiers`, and cannot set `cached_input_unpriced` or `cache_write_unpriced` to true, because it prices no tokens. Each entry prices only its own basis; a request that reports none of it is unpriced: it costs zero and is logged, like an unpriced model. |
| `nanodollars_per_character` | integer; minimum 0 | no | none | Required for `basis: characters`, and not allowed otherwise. The price of one character of the speech request's `input`, in nanodollars (15 USD per million characters is `15000`). A character is one Unicode code point after JSON unescaping. The request is charged this price times its characters, rounded up to a whole micro-USD. |
| `nanodollars_per_second` | integer; minimum 0 | no | none | Required for `basis: audio_seconds`, and not allowed otherwise. The price of one second of audio, in nanodollars (0.006 USD per minute is `100000`). The duration comes from the response: `usage.seconds` of a `duration` usage, else `usage.prompt_audio_seconds`, else the top-level `duration` of a `verbose_json` response. It is priced per millisecond and rounded up to a whole nanodollar, with no minimum duration. |
| `image_prices` | array of [ImagePrice](#imageprice); minimum items 1 | no | none | Required for `basis: images`, and not allowed otherwise. The most specific matching row prices each image: a row naming both `size` and `quality` first, then one naming one, then one naming neither. A request matches a row when each attribute the row names equals the value in the response, or in the request body when the response does not echo it. Values are plain strings matched exactly. A request that matches no row is unpriced: it costs zero and is logged, like an unpriced model. Two rows of the same specificity that one request could match are a load error: identical `size` and `quality` pairs, or a row naming only `size` beside a row naming only `quality`. |
| `cached_input_unpriced` | boolean | no | `false` | Requests reporting cached input remain unpriced. |
| `cache_write_unpriced` | boolean | no | `false` | Requests reporting cache creation remain unpriced. |
| `provider_type` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | The provider type the price applies to, for example `openai` or `anthropic`. Matches the `type` of the provider that served the request, set or inferred from its name. |
| `model` | string; minimum length 1 | yes | none | The model name, matched exactly and case-sensitively against the selected model: the upstream model name for the provider that served the request, or the requested model when no mapping applies. |
| `tier_mode` | one of `whole_request`, `graduated` | no | none | Required for `basis: tokens`, and not allowed for `images`. How `tiers` price a request. `whole_request`: the band selected by the input context size prices every token of the request. `graduated`: each context token costs the rate of the band that holds its position, and output tokens cost the rate of the band the whole context selects. No default, because the two modes give different prices. |
| `tiers` | array of [PricingTier](#pricingtier); minimum items 1 | no | none | Required for `basis: tokens`, and not allowed for `images`. The price bands, in increasing `up_to` order; exactly one band, the last, leaves `up_to` out. |

Any other field is a load error.

Rules:

- When `basis` is `images`: `image_prices` must be set. None of `tier_mode`, `tiers`, `nanodollars_per_character`, `nanodollars_per_second` is set.
- When `basis` is `characters`: `nanodollars_per_character` must be set. None of `tier_mode`, `tiers`, `image_prices`, `nanodollars_per_second` is set.
- When `basis` is `audio_seconds`: `nanodollars_per_second` must be set. None of `tier_mode`, `tiers`, `image_prices`, `nanodollars_per_character` is set.
- When `basis` is not `images`, `characters` or `audio_seconds`: `tier_mode`, `tiers` must be set. None of `image_prices`, `nanodollars_per_character`, `nanodollars_per_second` is set.

| `image_output_nanodollars_per_token` | integer; minimum 0 | no | none | The price of one image output token, in nanodollars. Set it on every band of the entry or on none. |
| `audio_input_nanodollars_per_token` | integer; minimum 0 | no | none | The price of one audio input token, in nanodollars. Set it on every band of the entry or on none. |
| `audio_output_nanodollars_per_token` | integer; minimum 0 | no | none | The price of one audio output token, in nanodollars. Set it on every band of the entry or on none. |

Any other field is a load error.

## Value types

### HostPort

Type: string; pattern `^([0-9A-Za-z_.-]+|\[[0-9A-Fa-f:.]+\]):[0-9]{1,5}$`.

A bind address in `host:port` form. IPv6 hosts use brackets: `[::1]:8080`.

Used at: `listen`, `admin`, `listen.address`.

Examples: `0.0.0.0:8080`, `127.0.0.1:9901`, `[::]:8080`.

### Duration

Type: string; pattern `^[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h)$`.

A duration: integer plus unit — `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), or `h` (hours).

Used at: `listen.request_headers_timeout`, `listen.request_timeout`, `listen.stream_idle_timeout`, `listen.max_stream_duration`, `auth.max_policy_staleness`, `auth.stored_output_owner_ttl`, `providers.<name>.connect_timeout`, `routes[].idle_timeout`, `ledger.group_commit_interval`, `providers.<name>.oauth2_jwt_bearer.assertion_lifetime`, `providers.<name>.oauth2_jwt_bearer.refresh_before`, `providers.<name>.oauth2_jwt_bearer.timeout`, `providers.<name>.outlier_detection.base_ejection_time`, `providers.<name>.outlier_detection.max_ejection_time`, `observability.metrics.export_interval`, `observability.metrics.export_deadline`, `observability.traces.max_age`, `observability.traces.segment_max_age`, `observability.tracing.export_deadline`, `auth.jwt[].jwks.refresh_interval`, `observability.traces.s3.upload_timeout`, `guardrails.default.http.timeout`.

Examples: `500ms`, `30s`, `5m`, `1h`.

### ProviderModelRef

Type: string; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*(/[^\s]+)?$`.

A provider reference: `provider-name`, or `provider-name/model-name`. In a `models.<name>.providers` entry the model part is applied, like `ModelProvider.model`. In `routes[].provider` and `routes[].fallbacks` it is accepted but not applied yet: the request's original model name is forwarded, and the load emits a warning naming the field.

Used at: `models.<name>.providers[]`, `routes[].provider`, `routes[].fallbacks[]`.

Examples: `openai`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `local-vllm/llama-3.3-70b`.

### ModelPattern

Type: string; minimum length 1.

A glob matched against the request's `model` field (the JSON body field for chat/completions APIs; the `model` query parameter for realtime WebSocket endpoints). `*` matches any run of characters; matching is case-sensitive. `*` alone matches every request.

Used at: `routes[].model`, `limits[].models[]`.

Examples: `gpt-5`, `gpt-5*`, `claude-*`, `llama-*`, `*`.

### TokenAmount

Type: integer (minimum 1) or string (pattern `^[0-9]+(k|m)$`).

A token count: a plain integer, or a string with `k` (thousands) / `m` (millions) suffix.

Used at: `limits[].tokens_per_minute`, `limits[].requests_per_minute`.

Examples: `8000`, `100k`, `2m`.
